chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: How studio dates were staffed and run in one take
summary: Leaders hand-picked reliable men; they tuned up, ran each tune down once and recorded a single take, often without music.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Like doing these recording dates -- these are very rare dates. You would get --
Like, if you were in New York, like they would call like the top musicians around to record. They'd pick certain guys that knew, you know, that they
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

wouldn't have any trouble with. Like, see those names there that you have, they were picked -- these are all picked men to do this date. These are just not guys that call downtown and say get me a saxophone player. They knew who they wanted. They'd call, "Look, we were doing a date on so and so and so." Well, they would call certain musicians for this date. And this would be it. We'd walk in and tune up and skim down he stuff one time and one take. That was it. No two and three takes. We'd run it down for the musicians and arrangements, and run it down for the vocalist, then run it down one more together. And boom, let's make it. That was it. Then we run down the next one, you know, and set it up. Teddy will make the introduction, come in there (inaudible) come in here, come in there you're going to do so and so. Sometimes we didn't have no music -- we
